text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:

- Slovenia will file a protest against Yugoslavia's decision to privatise property of Slovene citizens and companies, said Miran Mejak head of Slovenia's delegations in ex-Yugoslav assets division talks.

- According to Italian daily Il Piccolo, Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko will increase its power by six percent after it replaces its two steam generators. The new generators will be supplied by Siemens and Italian Ansaldo.
- Slovenia's biggest petrol trader Petrol demands a petrol price increase of 12 percent. The government is expected to decide on the matter by end of Septemeber.
- Number of unemployed Slovenians in June compared to May rose by 0.1 percent to 122,613, the Employment Office reported.

- Slovenia's largest bank Nova Ljubljanska Banka said it will give a loan of 24.2 million marks to Russian company Mosnegro for construction of a business block. The total amount of the investment is 28.5 million marks.
- Over 36,200 unemployed persons received compensation from Slovenia's Employment Office in June, the office said, the highest gross amount paid was 112,552 tolars ($662).
- Police seized three kilos of heroine and arrested five dealers in the coastal town of Koper on Wednesday.
- Slovenia's only airline Adria said on Wednesday it had increased its July passenger numbers by five percent to 79,000.
- Slovenian prosecutors introduced charity payment as punishment. Convicts will have to pay a certain amount stipulated by the court to contribute toward the building of a new hospital in Ljubljana.
